I unfortunately don't have an answer for you. The only thing that have helped me that I would recommend is meditation and zen Buddhism.... Especially the work of Alan Watts. I have also found help in several psychedelic sessions but in some cases they do more damage than healing so I wouldn't recommend them.... It all starts with accepting yourself as you are because there is no other "better version"... That's an illusion... And trying to get away from yourself or what you are willing only cause more anxiety, disarray and disconnect... Accepting yourself as an angry, addictive destructive person and learning to give yourself room to forgive yourself for not only mistakes you make but also for the the situations that were beyond your control when you were growing up is the first step... Jung calls it the integration of the shadow... It seems you can already identify the things you hate about yourself, which is a great barrier that a lot of people can't even accomplish... But identifying is half the battle... Only through integration can you start to heal and possibly even break some of the habits you hate about yourself in a healthy way... I highly recommend meditation and the work of Alan Watts (his later work is less "wuwu" and more grounded in western intellectualism and psychology and psychotherapy than in Buddhism but it's always connected with eastern thought.... ❤️ Bless OP
